sections.content: Reported speech introduces another person's words through verbs such as *decir*, *afirmar* and *declarar*. The basic structure is subject + reporting verb + *que* + reported statement. When the reporting verb is in the past, the verb inside the statement moves back: the present becomes the *imperfecto* («No conozco los detalles» → *dijo que no conocía los detalles*), the *indefinido* or *perfecto* becomes the *pluscuamperfecto* («He visto una luz» → *afirmó que había visto una luz*) and the future becomes the conditional («Hablaré mañana» → *dijo que hablaría al día siguiente*). You know the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 21, the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1 and the conditional from A2 Unit 26. Here you report statements only.

items.spanish: El periodista dijo que el objeto había aparecido sobre la ciudad.
items.english: The journalist said that the object had appeared over the city.

items.spanish: La testigo afirmó que había visto una luz desde su ventana.
items.english: The witness stated that she had seen a light from her window.

items.spanish: El alcalde declaró que no conocía todos los detalles.
items.english: The mayor stated that he did not know all the details.

items.spanish: Circulaba un rumor que decía que el fenómeno podía repetirse.
items.english: A rumour was circulating saying that the phenomenon could happen again.

items.spanish: El alcalde dijo que hablaría con los vecinos al día siguiente.
items.english: The mayor said that he would speak with the neighbours the next day.

sections.content: The basic reported-speech pattern is *decir* / *afirmar* / *declarar* + *que* + statement. Keep the reported statement grammatically consistent with its time reference.
